###from previous nrc sentiments, the most common emotions were trust(mother, food), fear( hunting, jaws ), anger (droping positive and negative)


```{r}
library(here)
library(dplyr)

if (!exists("fw_nrc" )){
  load(here("data/fw_nrc.rda"))
}
if (!exists("finn_clean" )){
  load(here("data/finn_clean.rda"))
}

fw_nrc$title_short <- paste("Ch", fw_nrc$chapter)

title_translate <- fw_nrc |> 
  group_by(chapter, title_short) |> 
  summarize(n_tokens = n(), .groups = "drop")
max(fw_nrc$chapter, na.rm = TRUE)
tail(title_translate)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Create the wide matrix from your existing fw_nrc data
nrc_wide <- fw_nrc |>
  # 1. Drop generic positive/negative to focus purely on the 8 core emotions
  filter(!sentiment %in% c("positive", "negative")) |>
  
  # 2. Count how many of each emotion appear in each chapter
  count(chapter, sentiment) |>
  
  # 3. Calculate the percentage of each emotion per chapter
  group_by(chapter) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) |>
  select(-n) |>
  
  # 4. PIVOT WIDER: This creates the actual matrix!
  # It turns the 'sentiment' column into 8 separate columns
  pivot_wider(names_from = sentiment, values_from = prop, values_fill = 0) |>
  as.data.frame()

# 5. The clustering algorithm requires the row names to be the chapter labels
rownames(nrc_wide) <- paste("Chapter", nrc_wide$chapter)
nrc_wide <- nrc_wide |> select(-chapter)

# Take a peek at your beautiful new matrix!
head(nrc_wide)
```
### some insight on the top sentiments and how they progress over the chapters.
